customConcept.name: Jumbo Kingdom
customConcept.blurb: Hong Kong's floating palace in Aberdeen Harbour: two boats of Cantonese seafood, dim sum and banquets, a dragon throne, and a shuttle boat to the door.

state.circumstances: In this Hong Kong, Jumbo never left. You're managing director of Aberdeen Restaurant Enterprises, the Melco subsidiary that owns Jumbo and Tai Pak, and you run both boats, the shuttle fleet and the kitchens for a salary and a share of the profit.

features.name: The Dragon Court and the dragon throne
features.pitch: The imperial-palace dining floor, with a carved dragon throne guests queue to be photographed on.

features.name: Tai Pak Floating Restaurant
features.pitch: Jumbo's older, smaller sister boat moored alongside, used for banquets and overflow.

features.name: Top Deck
features.pitch: A Western seafood bar and brunch spot on the roof deck, with harbour views and a drinks list.

features.name: Shuttle boats from Aberdeen
features.pitch: Free boats every few minutes from the Aberdeen Promenade and Shum Wan Pier; the ride is part of the night out.

features.name: Live seafood tanks
features.pitch: Tanks of fish and shellfish where guests choose their dinner before it's cooked.

setting.name: Shum Wan, Aberdeen Harbour
setting.desc: Moored in the Aberdeen typhoon shelter off Shum Wan Pier Drive, between Aberdeen and Ap Lei Chau, a few minutes by the restaurant's shuttle boats from the promenade. Mainland tour groups at lunch, Hong Kong families for birthdays and wedding banquets, and tourists who came for the photo of the palace lit up at night.

ev.text: Chinese New Year: both boats booked for banquets, lion dancers on the pier and the dragon throne queue out the door.
Mainland Golden Week: tour coaches lined Shum Wan Pier Drive from ten in the morning.
Typhoon Signal No. 8 went up. The shuttle boats stopped and Jumbo closed for two days, with the crew doubling the moorings.

desk.title: A super typhoon is heading for Hong Kong
desk.text: The Observatory expects to raise Signal No. 10 within 36 hours. The marine crew wants to add storm moorings and clear both boats; the floor managers point out there are three wedding banquets booked this weekend.

choices.blurb: Two weeks closed and a large bill; the certificate is clean.

world.notes: This is an alternate timeline. In the real world, Jumbo Floating Restaurant opened in Aberdeen Harbour in 1976, after a fire during construction in 1971 killed 34 people, and with the older Tai Pak made up Jumbo Kingdom, owned by Melco International through Aberdeen Restaurant Enterprises. It had an imperial-palace interior with a dragon throne, free shuttle boats from Aberdeen and Shum Wan Pier, and more than 30 million guests over its life, from Queen Elizabeth II to Tom Cruise; films including Enter the Dragon (on Tai Pak), The God of Cookery and Contagion were shot there. The owner said it had lost money every year since 2013, with losses above HK$100 million. It closed in March 2020, an Ocean Park rescue plan fell through, and it was towed out on 14 June 2022 and capsized near the Paracel Islands a few days later. In THIS game none of that happened after 2020: Jumbo reopened after the pandemic, Melco kept it, and it's doing well in 2026 on Hong Kong's recovery (44.5 million visitors in 2024, 49.9 million in 2025). No full Jumbo menu with prices survives online; the dishes here are ones travel guides and reviews reported (har gow, char siu bao, cuttlefish cake, seafood rolls, lobster salad, steamed grouper, blanched shrimp, flaming drunken shrimp, Peking duck, swallow's nest soup, crab soup, the seafood set and the dim sum lunch set, mango rice balls, eight-treasure rice) plus a few Cantonese staples. Reported prices from the 2010s (drunken shrimp HK$130, swallow's nest soup HK$440, crab soups HK$80-130, a dim sum lunch set HK$201 and seafood set HK$339 around 2019) were raised about 25% for 2026. Seating (about 2,300 across both boats), sales, other menu prices, wages and costs are the game's estimates, shown in US dollars at about HK$7.8 to the dollar; the Hong Kong minimum wage is HK$43.1 an hour from May 2026 and the median food-service wage about HK$60. A 10% service charge replaces tipping. Staff names are invented.

profile.name: Melco International Development
profile.kind: Hong Kong-listed casino and leisure group (HKEX: 200)
profile.desc: Lawrence Ho's company, whose real business is casino resorts in Macau through Melco Resorts. It owns Jumbo and Tai Pak through Aberdeen Restaurant Enterprises, bought in the family's early days of Hong Kong leisure.
profile.personality: Proud of Jumbo as a piece of Hong Kong history and impatient with it as a business. Casino results in Macau decide how generous head office feels; a good year on the boats buys you room, a bad one brings questions about whether Melco should own a restaurant at all.

rep.name: Vivian Tse
rep.title: Vice president, non-gaming assets
rep.style: Polite, precise and always busy; she reads the monthly report on the ferry to Macau and replies with three questions.

desk.title: Melco is reviewing its non-core assets
desk.text: Head office is deciding which businesses outside casinos it should keep. Jumbo is on the list, and Vivian Tse wants a five-year plan by the end of the month.

Hong Kong.name: Hong Kong

alcohol.note: Restaurants need a liquor licence from the Liquor Licensing Board on top of the FEHD restaurant licence.

inspections.system: The Food and Environmental Hygiene Department licenses and inspects restaurants and runs a demerit-points system: too many points and the licence is suspended.

Hong Kong.mealTimes: Yum cha from early morning to mid-afternoon; a short lunch rush from about 12:30 to 2pm; dinner from about 7 to 9:30pm, later for banquets.
Hong Kong.customs: Tables share every dish from the middle, and banquets for weddings and birthdays are booked months ahead. Most full-service restaurants add a 10% service charge and a small tea charge per head; tipping beyond leaving the change is optional. Live seafood is picked from the tanks and priced by weight, and service is quick and brisk rather than chatty.
Hong Kong.labour: The Employment Ordinance sets a statutory minimum wage, rest days and statutory holidays, but no general overtime premium. Contracts end with notice or pay in lieu, and long-serving staff are owed severance or long-service payments.

United States.name: United States

alcohol.note: Licensed by the state; quotas in some cities.

inspections.system: County or city health department inspections; letter grades posted in some cities.

United States.mealTimes: Lunch around noon to 1pm, dinner from about 6 to 8pm.
United States.customs: Guests expect fast, attentive service, free tap water and refills, and a check brought on request. Tipping 18-22% is expected at table service.
United States.labour: At-will employment in most states; overtime after 40 hours a week; minimum wages set by state and city.
